verses: Othin: "Counsel me, Frigg, for I long to fare, And Vafthruthnir fain would find; fit wisdom old with the giant wise Myself would I seek to match."
Frigg: "Heerfather here at home would I keep, Where the gods together dwell; Amid all the giants an equal in might To Vafthruthnir know I none."
Othin: "Much have I fared, much have I found. Much have I got from the gods; And fain would I know how Vafthruthnir now Lives in his lofty hall."
Frigg: "Safe mayst thou go, safe come again, And safe be the way thou wendest! Father of men, let thy mind be keen When speech with the giant thou seekest."
The wisdom then of the giant wise
Forth did he fare to try; He found the hall | of the father of Im, And in forthwith went Ygg.
Othin: "Vafthruthnir, hail! | to thy hall am I come, For thyself I fain would see; And first would I ask | if wise thou art, Or, giant, all wisdom hast won."
Vafthruthnir: "Who is the man | that speaks to me, Here in my lofty hall? Forth from our dwelling | thou never shalt fare, Unless wiser than I thou art."
Othin: "Gagnrath they call me, | and thirsty I come From a journey hard to thy hall; Welcome I look for, | for long have I fared, And gentle greeting, giant."
Vafthruthnir: "Why standest thou there | on the floor whilst thou speakest? A seat shalt thou have in my hall;
Then soon shall we know | whose knowledge is more, The guest's or the sage's gray."
Othin: "If a poor man reaches | the home of the rich, Let him wisely speak or be still; For to him who speaks | with the hard of heart Will chattering ever work ill."
Vafthruthnir: "Speak forth now, Gagnrath, | if there from the floor Thou wouldst thy wisdom make known: What name has the steed | that each morn anew The day for mankind doth draw?"
Othin: "Skinfaxi is he, | the steed who for men The glittering day doth draw; The best of horses | to heroes he seems, And brightly his mane doth burn."
Vafthruthnir: "Speak forth now, Gagnrath, | if there from the floor
Thou wouldst thy wisdom make known: What name has the steed | that from East anew Brings night for the noble gods?"
Othin: "Hrimfaxi name they | the steed that anew Brings night for the noble gods; Each morning foam | from his bit there falls, And thence come the dews in the dales."
Vafthruthnir: "Speak forth now, Gagnrath, | if there from the floor Thou wouldst thy wisdom make known: What name has the river | that 'twixt the realms Of the gods and the giants goes?"
Othin spoke:
"Ifing is the river | that 'twixt the realms Of the gods and the giants goes; For all time ever | open it flows, No ice on the river there is."
Vafthruthnir: "Speak forth now, Gagnrath, | if there from the floor
Thou wouldst thy wisdom make known: What name has the field | where in fight shall meet Surt and the gracious gods?"
Othin: "Vigrith is the field | where in fight shall meet Surt and the gracious gods; A hundred miles | each way does it measure. And so are its boundaries set."
Vafthruthnir: "Wise art thou, guest! | To my bench shalt thou go, In our seats let us speak together; Here in the hall | our heads, O guest, Shall we wager our wisdom upon."
Othin: "First answer me well, | if thy wisdom avails, And thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: In earliest time | whence came the earth, Or the sky, thou giant sage?"
Vafthruthnir: "Out of Ymir's flesh | was fashioned the earth, And the mountains were made of his bones; The sky from the frost-cold | giant's skull, And the ocean out of his blood."
Othin: "Next answer me well, | if thy wisdom avails, And thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: Whence came the moon, | o'er the world of men That fares, and the flaming sun?"
Vafthruthnir: "Mundilferi is he | who begat the moon, And fathered the flaming sun; The round of heaven | each day they run, To tell the time for men."
Othin: "Third answer me well, | if wise thou art called, If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: Whence came the day, | o'er mankind that fares, Or night with the narrowing moon?"
Vafthruthnir: "The father of day | is Delling called, And the night was begotten by Nor; Full moon and old | by the gods were fashioned, To tell the time for men."
Othin: "Fourth answer me well, | if wise thou art called, If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: Whence did winter come, | or the summer warm, First with the gracious gods?"
Vafthruthnir: "Vindsval he was | who was winter's father, And Svosuth summer begat;"
Othin: "Fifth answer me well, | if wise thou art called, If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: What giant first | was fashioned of old, And the eldest of Ymir's kin?"
Vafthruthnir: "Winters unmeasured | ere earth was made Was the birth of Bergelmir; Thruthgelmir's son | was the giant strong, And Aurgelmir's grandson of old."
Othin: "Sixth answer me well, | if wise thou art called, If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: Whence did Aurgelmir come | with the giants' kin, Long since, thou giant sage?"
Vafthruthnir: "Down from Elivagar | did venom drop, And waxed till a giant it was;
And thence arose | our giants' race, And thus so fierce are we found."
Othin: "Seventh answer me well, | if wise thou art called, If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: How begat he children, | the giant grim, Who never a giantess knew?"
Vafthruthnir: "They say 'neath the arms | of the giant of ice Grew man-child and maid together; And foot with foot | did the wise one fashion A son that six heads bore."
Othin: "Eighth answer me well, | if wise thou art called, If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: What farthest back | dost thou bear in mind? For wide is thy wisdom, giant!"
Vafthruthnir: "Winters unmeasured | ere earth was made Was the birth of Bergelmir; This first knew I well, | when the giant wise In a boat of old was borne."
Othin: "Ninth answer me well, | if wise thou art called If thou knowest it, Vafthruthnir, now: Whence comes the wind | that fares o'er the waves Yet never itself is seen?"
Vafthruthnir: "In an eagle's guise | at the end of heaven Hraesvelg sits, they say; And from his wings | does the wind come forth To move o'er the world of men."
Othin: "Tenth answer me now, | if thou knowest all The fate that is fixed for the gods:
Whence came up Njorth | to the kin of the gods,-- (Rich in temples | and shrines he rules,--) Though of gods he was never begot?"
Vafthruthnir: "In the home of the Wanes | did the wise ones create him, And gave him as pledge to the gods; At the fall of the world | shall he fare once more Home to the Wanes so wise."
Othin: "Eleventh answer me well, | What men | in home Each day to fight go forth?"
Vafthruthnir: "The heroes all | in Othin's hall Each day to fight go forth;
They fell each other, | and fare from the fight All healed full soon to sit."

Othin: "Twelfth answer me now | how all thou knowest Of the fate that is fixed for the gods; Of the runes of the gods | and the giants' race The truth indeed dost thou tell, (And wide is thy wisdom, giant!)"

Vafthruthnir: "Of the runes of the gods | and the giants' race The truth indeed can I tell, (For to every world have I won;) To nine worlds came I, | to Niflhel beneath, The home where dead men dwell."
Othin: "Much have I fared, | much have I found, Much have I got of the gods: What shall live of mankind | when at last there comes The mighty winter to men?"
Vafthruthnir: "In Hoddmimir's wood | shall hide themselves Lif and Lifthrasir then;
The morning dews | for meat shall they have, Such food shall men then find."
Othin: "Much have I fared, | much have I found, Much have I got of the gods: Whence comes the sun | to the smooth sky back, When Fenrir has snatched it forth?"
Vafthruthnir: "A daughter bright | Alfrothul bears Ere Fenrir snatches her forth; Her mother's paths | shall the maiden tread When the gods to death have gone."
Othin: "Much have I fared, | much have I found, Much have I got of the gods: What maidens are they, | so wise of mind. That forth o'er the sea shall fare?"
Vafthruthnir: "O'er Mogthrasir's hill | shall the maidens pass, And three are their throngs that come; They all shall protect | the dwellers on earth, Though they come of the giants' kin."
Othin: "Much have I fared, | much have I found, Much have I got of the gods: Who then shall rule | the realm of the gods, When the fires of Surt have sunk?"
Vafthruthnir: "In the gods' home Vithar | and Vali shall dwell, When the fires of Surt have sunk; Mothi and Magni | shall Mjollnir have When Vingnir falls in fight."
Othin: "Much have I fared, | much have I found, Much have I got of the gods:
What shall bring the doom | of death to Othin, When the gods to destruction go?"
Vafthruthnir: "The wolf shall fell | the father of men, And this shall Vithar avenge; The terrible jaws | shall he tear apart, And so the wolf shall he slay."
Othin: "Much have I fared, | much have I found, Much have I got from the gods: What spake Othin himself | in the ears of his son, Ere in the bale-fire he burned?"

Vafthruthnir: "No man can tell | what in olden time Thou spak'st in the ears of thy son; With fated mouth | the fall of the gods And mine olden tales have I told; With Othin in knowledge | now have I striven, And ever the wiser thou art."
